verses.1:1: The word of the LORD that came to Micah the Morashtite during the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw regarding Samaria and Jerusalem.
verses.1:2: Hear, all you peoples; pay attention, earth and its fullness; and may the Lord GOD be a witness against you, the Lord from His holy temple.
verses.1:3: For see, the LORD is going out from His place, and He will descend and tread upon the high places of the earth.
verses.1:4: And the mountains will melt beneath Him, and the valleys will split apart, like wax before the fire, like water poured down a slope.
verses.1:5: All this is because of Jacob's transgression and because of the sins of the house of Israel. What is Jacob's transgression? Is it not Samaria? And what are the high places of Judah? Is it not Jerusalem?
verses.1:6: And I will make Samaria a ruin heap of the field, planting places for a vineyard; and I will pour down her stones into the valley and lay bare her foundations.
verses.1:7: All her carved images will be smashed to pieces, all her wages will be burned with fire, and I will make all her idols a desolation; for from the wages of a prostitute she gathered them, and to the wages of a prostitute they will return.
verses.1:8: Over this I will lament and wail; I will walk barefoot and naked; I will make a lamentation like the jackals and a mourning like the ostriches.
verses.1:9: For her wound is beyond cure, for it has come as far as Judah; it has reached up to the gate of my people, all the way to Jerusalem.
verses.1:10: Do not tell it in Gath; do not weep at all; in Beth-le-aphrah, roll yourself in the dust.
verses.1:11: Pass on your way, inhabitant of Shaphir, in nakedness and shame; the inhabitant of Zaanan has not gone out; the lamentation of Beth-ezel will take from you its standing place.
verses.1:12: For the inhabitant of Maroth is in anguish for good, because calamity has come down from the LORD to the gate of Jerusalem.
verses.1:13: Hitch the chariot to the swift steeds, inhabitant of Lachish; she was the beginning of sin for the daughter of Zion, because the transgressions of Israel were found in you.
verses.1:14: Therefore you will give farewell gifts for Moresheth-gath; the houses of Achzib will be a deception to the kings of Israel.
verses.1:15: Once more I will bring the conqueror to you, inhabitant of Mareshah; the glory of Israel will come as far as Adullam.
verses.1:16: Make yourself bald and shear your hair over the children of your delight; widen your baldness like the vulture, for they have gone into exile from you.
verses.2:1: Woe to those who devise iniquity and contrive evil on their beds! By the light of morning they carry it out, because it lies in the power of their hand.
verses.2:2: They covet fields and snatch them away, and houses, and carry them off; they defraud a man and his household, and a man and his inheritance.
verses.2:3: Therefore this is what the LORD says: "Look, against this family I am devising a calamity from which you will not remove your necks, and you will not walk loftily, for it is a time of calamity."
verses.2:4: In that day one will lift up a taunt against you and wail a grievous lament, saying, "We are totally devastated! He exchanges the portion of my people; how He removes it from me! To an apostate He apportions our fields."
verses.2:5: Therefore you will have no one who casts a measuring cord by lot in the assembly of the LORD.
verses.2:6: "Do not preach!" they preach. They will not preach about these things; disgrace will not turn back.
verses.2:7: Should it be said, house of Jacob, "Has the Spirit of the LORD grown impatient? Are these His deeds?" Do My words not do good to the one who walks uprightly?
verses.2:8: Yet recently My people have risen up as an enemy; from over the garment you strip the mantle, from those passing by in safety, those averse to war.
verses.2:9: You drive out the women of My people, each from her house of delight; from her little children you take My majesty forever.
verses.2:10: Get up and go, for this is not the resting place; because it is defiled, it brings destruction, even a severe destruction.
verses.2:11: If a man walking in wind and falsehood should lie, "I will preach to you about wine and strong drink," he would be the preacher of this people.
verses.2:12: I will surely assemble all of you, Jacob; I will surely gather the remnant of Israel. I will place them together like sheep in a fold, like a flock in the midst of its pasture; they will clamor with people.
verses.2:13: The one who breaks through goes up ahead of them; they break through and pass the gate and go out by it; their king passes ahead of them, and the LORD is at their head.
verses.3:1: Then I said, "Please hear, heads of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel! Is it not yours to know justice?
verses.3:2: You who hate good and love evil, who tear their skin away from them and their flesh off their bones,
verses.3:3: and who eat the flesh of my people, strip their skin off them, shatter their bones, and chop them up like what is in the pot, like meat in the middle of a cauldron.
verses.3:4: Then they will cry out to the LORD, yet He will not answer them, and He will conceal His face from them in that time, because they have made their deeds evil."
verses.3:5: This is what the LORD says regarding the prophets who lead my people astray, who bite with their teeth and call out, "Peace," yet against anyone who puts nothing into their mouths, they consecrate war:
verses.3:6: "Therefore it will be night for you, without vision, and it will grow dark for you, without divining; the sun will set on the prophets, and the day will turn black over them.
verses.3:7: The seers will be put to shame, and the diviners will be disgraced; all of them will cover their upper lip, because there is no answer from God."
verses.3:8: Yet I myself am full of power, by the Spirit of the LORD, and of justice and might, to tell Jacob his transgression and Israel his sin.
verses.3:9: Please hear this, heads of the house of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel, who loathe justice and pervert all that is straight,
verses.3:10: building Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with injustice.
verses.3:11: Her heads judge for a bribe, her priests give instruction for a price, and her prophets divine for silver; yet they lean on the LORD, saying, "Is the LORD not in our midst? No calamity will come upon us."
verses.3:12: Therefore, on account of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will become ruin heaps, and the mountain of the house will become high places of a forest.
verses.4:1: And it will happen at the end of the days that the mountain of the house of the LORD will be firmly established at the head of the mountains, and it will be raised higher than the hills, and peoples will stream to it.
verses.4:2: And many nations will go and say, "Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD and to the house of the God of Jacob, so that He may instruct us concerning His ways and we may walk in His paths." For from Zion instruction will go out, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.
verses.4:3: And He will judge between many peoples and arbitrate for strong nations far away; and they will hammer their swords into plow blades and their spears into pruning knives. Nation will not raise a sword against nation, and they will no longer learn war.
verses.4:4: And they will sit, each person beneath his vine and beneath his fig tree, and there will be no one to frighten them; for the mouth of the LORD of hosts has spoken.
verses.4:5: For all the peoples walk, each person in the name of his god, yet we ourselves will walk in the name of the LORD our God forever and ever.
verses.4:6: "On that day," declares the LORD, "I will gather the limping and assemble the outcast, and those whom I have afflicted.
verses.4:7: And I will make the limping into a remnant and the one driven far away into a strong nation; and the LORD will reign over them on Mount Zion from this time on and forever."
verses.4:8: And you, tower of the flock, fortified hill of daughter Zion, to you it will come, and the former dominion will arrive, the kingdom belonging to daughter Jerusalem.
verses.4:9: Now why do you raise an outcry? Is there no king within you, or has your counselor perished, that writhing pain has taken hold of you like a woman giving birth?
verses.4:10: Writhe and push forth, daughter Zion, like a woman giving birth; for now you will go out from the city and dwell in the open field, and you will come as far as Babylon. There you will be rescued; there the LORD will redeem you from the grasp of your enemies.
verses.4:11: And now many nations have gathered together against you, saying, "Let her be desecrated, and let our eyes gloat over Zion."
verses.4:12: Yet they do not know the designs of the LORD, nor have they understood His counsel, that He has assembled them like sheaves to the threshing floor.
verses.4:13: Rise up and thresh, daughter Zion, for I will make your horn iron and I will make your hooves bronze; and you will crush many peoples, and I will devote their unjust gain to the LORD and their wealth to the Lord of all the earth.
verses.4:14: Now gather yourself in troops, daughter of troops; a siege has been set against us; with a rod they will strike the judge of Israel on the cheek.
verses.5:1: And you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, too small to be among the thousands of Judah, from you one will come out for Me to be ruler in Israel, and his origins are from antiquity, from days of long ago.
verses.5:2: Therefore He will hand them over until the time a woman in labor has given birth, and the remainder of his brothers will return to the sons of Israel.
verses.5:3: And he will stand and shepherd in the might of the LORD, in the grandeur of the name of the LORD his God. And they will remain, for now he will grow great as far as the ends of the earth.
verses.5:4: And this one will be peace. When Assyria enters our land and when he treads in our citadels, we will raise up against him seven shepherds and eight princes of humankind.
verses.5:5: And they will shepherd the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod within its gateways; and he will rescue us from Assyria when he enters our land and when he treads within our border.
verses.5:6: And the remnant of Jacob will be in the midst of many peoples like dew from the LORD, like rain showers upon grass, which does not wait for a man nor linger for the sons of humankind.
verses.5:7: And the remnant of Jacob will be among the nations, in the midst of many peoples, like a lion among the animals of the forest, like a young lion among flocks of sheep, which, if it passes through, tramples and tears apart, with no one to rescue.
verses.5:8: May your hand be raised high over your adversaries, and may all your enemies be cut off.
verses.5:9: "And it will happen on that day," declares the LORD, "that I will cut off your horses from your midst and I will destroy your chariots.
verses.5:10: And I will cut off the cities of your land and demolish all your fortresses.
verses.5:11: And I will cut off sorceries from your hand, and you will have no fortune-tellers.
verses.5:12: And I will cut off your carved images and your standing stones from your midst, and you will never again bow down to the work of your hands.
verses.5:13: And I will uproot your Asherah poles from your midst and wipe out your cities.
verses.5:14: And in anger and fury I will carry out vengeance against the nations that did not listen."
verses.6:1: Listen now to what the LORD is saying: "Stand up, argue the case before the mountains, and may the hills hear your voice."
verses.6:2: Listen, mountains, to the LORD's lawsuit, and you steadfast foundations of the earth; for the LORD has a lawsuit with His people, and He will argue His case with Israel.
verses.6:3: "My people, what have I done to you, and in what way have I wearied you? Testify against Me.
verses.6:4: For I brought you up out of the land of Egypt, and from the house of slaves I ransomed you; and I sent ahead of you Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.
verses.6:5: My people, remember now what Balak king of Moab planned and what Balaam son of Beor answered him, from Shittim to Gilgal, in order to know the righteous deeds of the LORD."
verses.6:6: "With what shall I approach the LORD, bow low before God on high? Shall I approach Him with burnt offerings, with year-old calves?
verses.6:7: Will the LORD take pleasure in thousands of rams, in tens of thousands of streams of oil? Shall I give my firstborn for my rebellion, the fruit of my body for my soul's sin?"
verses.6:8: He has declared to you, mortal, what is good; and what is the LORD requiring from you except to practice justice, to love steadfast kindness, and to walk in humility with your God?
verses.6:9: The voice of the LORD calls out to the city, and sound wisdom perceives Your name: "Heed the rod and the One who has appointed it!
verses.6:10: Are there still in the house of the wicked treasures of wickedness, and a scant ephah that is cursed?
verses.6:11: Can I be pure with scales of wickedness and with a pouch of deceptive stone weights?
verses.6:12: For her wealthy people are full of violence, her residents speak falsehood, and their tongue is deceitful in their mouth.
verses.6:13: So I also have made you sick by striking you, leaving you desolate because of your sins.
verses.6:14: You will eat, yet you will not be satisfied, and your emptiness will remain inside you; you will carry off, yet you will not rescue, and whatever you do rescue I will hand over to the sword.
verses.6:15: You will sow, yet you will not harvest; you will tread olives, yet you will not rub oil on yourself, and tread new wine, yet you will not drink wine.
verses.6:16: For the statutes of Omri are kept, along with every practice of the house of Ahab, and you walked in their counsels, so that I make you a desolation and her residents an object of hissing; and you will bear the disgrace of My people."
verses.7:1: Woe to me, for I have become like the gatherings of summer fruit, like the gleanings of the grape harvest; there is not a cluster to eat, nor an early fig that my soul craves.
verses.7:2: The devout one has perished from the land, and there is no upright person among humankind; all of them lie in ambush for bloodshed; each man hunts his brother with a net.
verses.7:3: Both hands are on evil to do it skillfully: the official asks, and the judge asks for a payoff, and the prominent man speaks the craving of his soul; and they twist it together.
verses.7:4: Their best is like a brier, the most upright worse than a thorn hedge. The day of your watchmen, your reckoning, has come; now will be their bewilderment.
verses.7:5: Do not put trust in a neighbor; do not rely on a close friend; from her who lies in your embrace, guard the doorways of your mouth.
verses.7:6: For a son disdains a father, a daughter rises against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; the enemies of a man are the men of his house.
verses.7:7: Yet I will keep watch for the LORD; I will hope in the God of my salvation; my God will hear me.
verses.7:8: Do not rejoice over me, my enemy! Though I have fallen, I will rise up; though I sit in darkness, the LORD is a light to me.
verses.7:9: I will bear the LORD's indignation, for I have sinned against Him, until He argues my case and renders justice for me. He will bring me out into the light; I will gaze upon His righteousness.
verses.7:10: And my enemy will see, and shame will cover her, the one who said to me, "Where is the LORD your God?" My eyes will gaze upon her; now she will be trampled underfoot like mud of the streets.
verses.7:11: A day to build your walls! On that day the boundary will extend far.
verses.7:12: On that day they will come to you from Assyria and the cities of Egypt, and from Egypt as far as the River, and from sea to sea, and from mountain to mountain.
verses.7:13: Yet the earth will become a desolation on account of its inhabitants, from the fruit of their deeds.
verses.7:14: Shepherd Your people with Your rod, the flock of Your inheritance, dwelling alone in a woodland in the midst of fertile land; may they graze in Bashan and Gilead as in ancient days.
verses.7:15: As in the days of your coming out from the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders.
verses.7:16: The nations will see and be ashamed of all their strength; they will place a hand over the mouth; their ears will grow deaf.
verses.7:17: They will lick dust like a serpent; like creeping things of the earth, they will come trembling from their enclosures; they will turn in dread toward the LORD our God, and they will fear You.
verses.7:18: Who is a God like You, who forgives iniquity and passes over rebellion for the remnant of His inheritance? He does not hold fast to His anger forever, for He delights in loyal love.
verses.7:19: He will again show us compassion; He will subdue our iniquities; and You will hurl all their sins into the depths of the sea.
verses.7:20: You will give faithfulness to Jacob, loyal love to Abraham, which You swore to our fathers from days of old.

notes.1:5: MT reads plural בָּמוֹת ("high places"), retained here rather than emending to "sin" with some ancient versions.
notes.1:8: Translates the Qere שׁוֹלָל ("barefoot," lit. "stripped"); the Ketiv שילל is a rare variant spelling of the same word.
notes.1:9: Hebrew construes the plural noun מַכּוֹתֶיהָ ("her wounds") with a feminine singular predicate and verb, then shifts to masculine singular נָגַע ("it has reached").
notes.1:10: Translates the Qere הִתְפַּלָּשִׁי ("roll yourself," Hithpael imperative 2fs); the Ketiv התפלשתי is 1cs perfect ("I have rolled myself"). Beth-le-aphrah ("house of dust") plays on עָפָר ("dust"), initiating a chain of town-name wordplays through v. 15.
notes.1:11: The final clause is notoriously obscure in MT; עֶמְדָּתוֹ is a hapax legomenon from עמד ("to stand"), literally "its standing place" or "support."
notes.2:4: נִהְיָה is difficult; it may intensify נְהִי ("a grievous lament") or be Niphal perfect of הָיָה ("It is done!"). שׁוֹבֵב denotes a rebellious or apostate person, here apparently the foreign invader.
notes.2:6: Hiphil נטף literally means "drip," used idiomatically for prophetic preaching (also v. 11). יִסַּג is Qal imperfect of נסג ("turn back/depart"); some connect it with נשׂג ("overtake"), reading the second half as part of the opponents' quote ("disgrace will not overtake us").
notes.2:10: MT vocalizes טָמְאָה as Qal perfect 3fs ("it is defiled") rather than the noun טֻמְאָה ("uncleanness"), followed by Piel תְּחַבֵּל ("it brings destruction") and cognate חֶבֶל נִמְרָץ ("a severe destruction").
notes.2:12: בָּצְרָה (pointed botsrah) means "enclosure/fold," paralleling דֹּבֶר ("pasture"), though some take it as the place name Bozrah. MT הַדָּבְרוֹ unusually combines the definite article with a 3ms possessive suffix ("its pasture").
notes.3:2: Translates the Qere רָע (masculine "evil," matching טוֹב "good"); the Ketiv רעה is the feminine form רָעָה.
notes.3:3: פִּצֵּחוּ (Piel of פצח, "shatter/break in pieces") occurs only here in this sense. MT reads כַּאֲשֶׁר בַּסִּיר ("like what is in the pot") rather than "like flesh in the pot" as in the Septuagint.
notes.3:6: MT vocalizes וְחָשְׁכָה as a Qal weqatal 3fs verb ("and it will grow dark") rather than a noun ("darkness"), followed by the infinitive מִקְּסֹם ("without divining").
notes.3:8: אֶת־רוּחַ יְהֹוָה is uniquely prefixed with אֵת among the listed qualities, functioning as the preposition "with/by" to mark the Spirit of the LORD as the source of Micah's power.
notes.3:12: עִיִּין ("ruin heaps") uses the plural ending -in (cf. עִיִּים in Jer 26:18); "the mountain of the house" (הַר הַבַּיִת) refers to the temple mount.
notes.4:7: The word translated "the one driven far away" is a Hebrew hapax legomenon, a Niphal feminine singular participle of a denominative verb derived from the adverb meaning "farther" or "beyond."
notes.4:13: The MT reads the Hiphil verb as first person singular ("I will devote," with the LORD speaking of Himself in the third person, as in 4:7); some grammarians analyze the -ti ending as an archaic second person feminine singular ("you will devote"), matching the preceding verb.
notes.4:14: The Hithpolel verb translated "gather yourself in troops" plays on the noun "troops" (gedud) and can alternatively mean "gash yourself" in mourning, reflecting two senses of the Hebrew root gadad.
notes.5:1: The term "thousands" denotes tribal and military clans of Judah. Literally "origins" is "goings out" (from the same root as "come out"), and "days of long ago" can also mean "days of eternity."
notes.5:5: The verb "shepherd" continues the shepherd imagery of 5:3-4 in an ironic military sense. The phrase "within its gateways" renders the MT literally (plural of the noun for entrance or doorway with a feminine singular suffix referring to the land of Nimrod).
notes.5:13: The MT reads "your cities" (as in 5:10), though the identical Hebrew form is occasionally understood as a homonym meaning "your adversaries" (cf. Ps 139:20).
notes.6:9: The MT vocalizes the verb in the middle clause as Qal imperfect of ra'ah ("perceives" or "sees"), though many interpreters understand it as a variant form of the root meaning "to fear" ("it is sound wisdom to fear Your name"). The Hebrew noun translated "rod" can also mean "tribe."
notes.6:10: The interrogative form translated "Are there" uses a rare Hebrew variant (ish) of the standard particle of existence (yesh), as in 2 Samuel 14:19. An "ephah" was a dry grain measure.
notes.6:11: The MT vocalizes the verb as Qal imperfect ("Can I be pure?"), expressing either a rhetorical question from the merchant's standpoint or the LORD's refusal to remain blameless while tolerating fraud; it can also be repointed as Piel ("Can I acquit?").
notes.6:13: The MT vocalizes the verb as Hiphil perfect of chalah ("make sick" or "inflict a grievous blow"), whereas several ancient versions read a similar root meaning "begin."
notes.6:14: The noun translated "emptiness" is a Hebrew hapax legomenon widely understood as gnawing hunger or emptiness. The following Hiphil verb literally means "move away" or "remove."
notes.6:16: The MT opens with a passive Hithpael verb ("are kept"), shifts to a third person feminine singular suffix ("her residents," referring back to the city of 6:9 and 6:12), and reads "My people" rather than the Septuagint's "the peoples."
notes.7:3: The opening clause is notably terse (literally "upon evil are both hands, to do well," with לְהֵיטִיב Hiphil infinitive construct of יטב). The final verb וַיְעַבְּתוּהָ is a Piel hapax legomenon from עבת (cognate with עֲבֹת, "cord"), picturing the corrupt leaders twisting the scheme together.
notes.7:12: מָצוֹר is the poetic singular designation for Egypt (as in 2 Kings 19:24; Isaiah 19:6), though the word can also mean "fortress," and נָהָר ("the River") denotes the Euphrates. The closing poetic merisms וְיָם מִיָּם וְהַר הָהָר literally read "and sea from sea, and mountain from the mountain."
notes.7:14: Anarthrous כַּרְמֶל can denote "fertile land" or "orchard" (paired with יַעַר, "woodland," as in Isaiah 29:17; 32:15), or the proper name "Carmel."
notes.7:15: The Masoretic text shifts from second-person singular צֵאתְךָ ("your coming out") to first-person divine speech with a third-person masculine singular object suffix in אַרְאֶנּוּ (Hiphil imperfect of ראה, "I will show him," referring collectively to the people of Israel).
notes.7:19: Following the Masoretic text strictly, the verse shifts from third person ("He") to second person ("You," Hiphil imperfect וְתַשְׁלִיךְ) and preserves the third-person plural suffix in חַטֹּאותָם ("their sins"), which several ancient versions harmonize to "our sins."
